description.narrative: Overall Goal: To create a model for private sector participation in policy advocacy and the implementation of smart and sustainableagriculture models in 2 provinces. Specific Objectives are to strengthen the capacity and create conditions for agriculture-relatedprivate sector entities in the 2 target provinces to be able to: - Access and participate in the development and advocacy of smart agriculture policies (Policy Advocacy Work). - Apply and disseminate knowledge on socially and environmentallyresponsible productionto farmers and consumers (Awareness Raising Work). Target Outcomes: - Private sector entities and agricultural enterprises in the target areas understand the policies, have the capacity, and participate effectively in proposing and driving smart agriculture policies (Policy Advocacy Work). - A forum for dialogue, knowledge exchange, and information sharing among the private sector, government, farmers, and consumers is established and functions continuously to promote the development of a policy bank (Knowledge and Networking Aspect). - Consumers and communities in the target areas are aware of and trust smart and sustainable agricultural products, leading to purchasing decisions that benefit health and the environment (Awareness Raising Work). - Activities and pilot models of sustainable production are established, operated jointly by the private sector and farmers, serving as useful models that can be scaledup (Practical Implementation Aspect). Main Activities: - Organizetraining for the private sector: Conduct specialized training courses on advocacy, marketing, and necessary equipment for target communities and competition winners (transferring knowledge from the private sector to the community). - Organize policy dialogue forums and knowledge exchange platforms: To connect the private sector,government representatives, farmers, and consumers to discuss and identify points for policy improvement. - Disseminate knowledge and raise consumer awareness: Through mass mediaand public events to promote the benefits of smart agriculture and products derived from responsible production. - Create and implement smart agriculture pilot projects: Organize competitions and award grants for creative and smart agricultural (farming) ideas from youth in the 2 provinces for climate-resilient agriculture during important events at the community level. This project will address the main problems by building knowledge and understanding, as demonstrated by datafrom the survey: o Basedon the high training needs identified by farmers (water management 65%, disease management 55%, soil healthimprovement 45%), the project will provide training on modern production techniques. For the private sector, training will focus onCSA principles, relevant policies, and socially responsible business models. o The project will establish dialogue platforms at theprovincial and district levels to address the lack of coordination (78%) highlighted by the survey. These platforms will serve as channels for the private sector and farmers to exchange lessons learned, build networks, and jointly plan production. o The project will support "model activities" implemented collaboratively by the private sector and farmer groups. These activities will be tangible models, such as: growing tomatoes in net houses (leveraging farmers' expertise), improving soil with organic fertilizer, or producing organic vegetables for markets in tourist areas (in Luang Prabang).

participating-org.narrative:
Association for Rural Mobilisation and Improvement (ARMI) is a Nationwide Membership Lao Civil Society Organization that was established in 2006 under the Lao Union of Science and Engineering Associations (LUSEA) and re-registered under the Ministryof Home Affairs (MoHA) license No. 511/MoHA on August 12, 2012. In May 2005, at the Lao member organization (LMO) meeting, it was discussed and agreed that "the CIDSE-Laos office needs to close by the end of 2008". Following that agreement, CIDSE-Laos’ staff has held many follow-up discussions. On April 3-4, the last workshop was held in the CIDSE Laos office. Fifteen CIDSE staff decided to set up a membership association registered under the Lao Union of Science and Engineering Associations (LUSEA) on October 10, 2006.
ARMI was re-registered on August 9, 2012, under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MoHA) and changed its name to "Association for Rural Mobilization andImprovement (ARMI)" in order to fit the decree No. 115/PM on the establishment of the association in Laos, which was approved on April 29, 2009.
Vision: ARMI aims to contribute to the well-being of all-ethnic groups based on mutual respect, equal opportunities, care for the environment, and the sustainable use of resources.
Mission: To build capacities amongst target groups to improve theirquality of life for their well-being in green and sustainable ways.
Target group: Rural communities and the poor and disadvantaged, especially children, youth, women, and people with disabilities (PWDs).
Values: Solidarity, Participation, Transparency, Effectiveness, and Opportunities for All
5 Years of Strategic Goals (2021-2025): 1. To reduce poverty by improving food security 2. To promote nutrition and sanitation for good health for all in communities 3. To protect the environment and natural resources in green andsustainable ways 4. To promote community participation for the quality of education 5. To promote community development with the participation of PWDs
